papers.title: Housing mice in thermoneutrality causes peripheral tissue-specific changes in the number, identity, and phase of circadian-expressed mRNA transcripts.
papers.abstract: Laboratory mice are typically housed at room temperature (20-25°C), well below their thermoneutral zone (about 30°C), imposing chronic mild cold stress that increases metabolic rate by 30-40%. Because circadian and metabolic physiology are highly temperature-sensitive, we tested whether this housing condition reshapes rhythmic gene expression in tissues central to cardiovascular and metabolic health. We hypothesized that mild cold stress suppresses circadian gene expression in peripheral tissues. We performed RNA sequencing on hearts, livers, and diaphragms collected every 4 hours over 48 hours in constant darkness from male mice to identify transcripts with approximately 24-hour rhythms. Thermoneutral housing reorganized the circadian transcriptome tissue-specifically. Out of ∼13000 filtered transcripts, the proportion of rhythmic transcripts (q<0.05) in the heart nearly quadrupled, from 11% (1410) at room temperature to 42% (5282) at thermoneutrality, while the diaphragm rose modestly (6% to 9%; 792 vs. 1153). The liver's overall proportion was unchanged (36% vs. 37%; 4041 vs. 4150), yet more than 30% of rhythmic transcripts were unique between housing conditions. Almost 80% of rhythmic genes in the heart under thermoneutrality show acrophase near the subjective activity/rest transition. Gene ontology analysis revealed coordinated changes in the temporal organization of metabolic pathways in the heart and liver but less pronounced in the diaphragm. These changes occurred without detectable changes in core clock expression, implicating regulators acting downstream of, or parallel to, the clock itself. Because room temperature housing is standard across biomedical research, our findings show that this overlooked variable can distort the circadian transcriptome of tissues central to cardiovascular and metabolic disease, with implications for how mouse studies model human physiology.
papers.journal: American journal of physiology. Cell physiology

papers.title: Cephalic and peripheral pain thresholds in migraine and tension-type headache: evidence for central sensitization and modulation by sleep physiology.
papers.abstract: Central sensitization understood as an increased responsiveness of central nociceptive neurons, has been implicated in migraine and tension-type headache (TTH). How sensitization differs by headache phenotypes and how sleep physiology relates to pain sensitivity remain unclear. We assessed pressure pain thresholds (PPT) at cephalic (temporalis, splenius, trapezius) and peripheral (distal finger) sites and heat/cold pain thresholds (HPT/CPT) at forehead and palmar hand in 33 interictal migraineurs - categorized as sleep-related (SM) or non-sleep-related (NSM) - and 20 TTH patients - episodic (ETTH) or chronic (CTTH) - versus age/sex-matched controls. Overnight polysomnography (PSG) quantified stage N3-sleep and a slow-burst (KD) index. Group differences used Mann-Whitney U (pre-specified contrasts) and Kruskal-Wallis; associations used Spearman correlations. NSM showed reduced PPT at splenius (p=0.001) and trapezius (p=0.011) and reduced thermal thresholds at palmar hand (HPT p=0.009; CPT p=0.031) vs. controls. In NSM, KD index correlated inversely with HPT at palmar hand and forehead (rho to -0.57; p≤0.04). In ETTH, N3-sleep correlated positively with frontal CPT (rho=0.86; p=0.01) and finger PPT (rho=0.76; p=0.03). Interictal NSM exhibits signs of central sensitization by hyperalgesia both cephalic and extra-cephalic, potentially modulated by sleep neurophysiology. Deep sleep may be protective in ETTH, whereas higher slow-burst activity relates to lower thermal thresholds in NSM.

papers.title: Alleviating Depressive Symptoms Through Continuous Positive Airway Pressure Therapy: Long-Term Effects on Patients with Obstructive Sleep Apnea.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) increases the risk of physical and psychological comorbidities, including depression. Although the short-term impact of continuous positive airway pressure (CPAP) therapy on depressive symptoms is established, its long-term psychological impact beyond 2 years remains underexplored. To evaluate the impact of long-term CPAP therapy on depressive symptoms in patients with OSA, focusing on Self-Rating Depression Scale (SDS) subdomain changes, as well as the influence of demographic and clinical variables such as age and sex. We enrolled 170 patients with OSA who underwent polysomnography and received CPAP for ≥ 6 months at the Nihon University Itabashi Hospital Sleep Center. Depression severity was measured using the SDS, and subgroup analyses assessed associations between changes in SDS scores and clinical parameters (age, sex, CPAP adherence, and sleep-related indices). Total SDS scores significantly declined from 40.2 to 37.5 in patients using CPAP for ≥2 years. Improvement was most pronounced in the cognitive and behavioral subdomains (e.g., fatigue, motivation, and decision-making) and was statistically significant among male patients, whereas female patients showed a nonsignificant trend toward improvement. No significant associations were observed between baseline characteristics (e.g., age and comorbidities) and SDS score changes. Multivariate analysis confirmed these improvements were not solely attributable to a single subdomain. Long-term CPAP therapy was associated with modest improvements in depressive symptoms in patients with OSA, particularly in cognitive and behavioral domains. In exploratory analyses, benefits appeared more evident in males, but these findings should be interpreted with caution given the limited female sample size.

papers.title: Cardiac remodeling, autonomic parameters, and clinical factors associated with obstructive sleep apnea: a case-control study.
papers.abstract: Obstructive sleep apnea (OSA) is associated with substantial cardiovascular morbidity through mechanisms involving intermittent hypoxia, sympathetic activation, oxidative stress, and progressive cardiac remodeling. The present study aimed to comprehensively evaluate clinical characteristics, echocardiographic abnormalities, autonomic function, and independent factors associated with OSA in a case-control population. This observational, case-control study included 108 adults recruited from a tertiary sleep laboratory, 54 patients with OSA and 54 controls selected using frequency matching for age and sex and considered at low risk for OSA based on STOP-Bang screening. Clinical characteristics, cardiovascular risk factors, transthoracic echocardiographic parameters, structural cardiac abnormalities, and 24-hour Holter-derived autonomic indices were compared between groups. Continuous variables were analyzed using the Mann-Whitney U test, categorical variables using Pearson's chi-square or Fisher's exact test, and univariable and multivariable binary logistic regression analyses were performed to identify variables independently associated with OSA. Compared with controls, patients with OSA had significantly higher prevalences of obesity, smoking, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, and ischemic heart disease (IHD). Echocardiography demonstrated larger left atrial and right ventricular diameters, higher pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), and increased frequencies of left ventricular hypertrophy (LVH), diastolic dysfunction, and moderate tricuspid regurgitation (TR). Among the Holter-derived autonomic parameters, the root mean square of successive differences between adjacent normal-to-normal intervals (RMSSD) was significantly lower in patients with OSA in the unadjusted comparison. In multivariable linear regression analyses, the association between OSA and RMSSD was attenuated and did not reach statistical significance, while OSA was not independently associated with the standard deviation of normal-to-normal intervals (SDNN). In univariable logistic regression analyses, obesity, smoking, hypertension, diabetes mellitus, ischemic heart disease, left ventricular hypertrophy, and diastolic dysfunction were significantly associated with OSA. After multivariable adjustment, obesity [adjusted odds ratio (OR) 10.86, 95% confidence intervals (CI) 2.99-39.47], smoking (adjusted OR 4.88, 95% CI 1.32-18.14), ischemic heart disease (adjusted OR 19.17, 95% CI 1.65-222.41), and left ventricular hypertrophy (adjusted OR 3.54, 95% CI 1.01-12.40) remained independently associated with OSA. OSA was associated with structural cardiovascular abnormalities and an unadjusted difference in the Holter-derived autonomic parameter RMSSD, whereas neither RMSSD nor SDNN showed a statistically significant independent association with OSA after multivariable adjustment. Obesity, smoking, ischemic heart disease, and left ventricular hypertrophy were independently associated with the presence of OSA, underscoring the close relationship between sleep-disordered breathing and cardiovascular disease. Comprehensive cardiovascular evaluation may improve risk stratification and support earlier identification of patients at increased cardiovascular risk.

papers.title: Intervention with Exogenous Melatonin Has No Adverse Effects on Cardiometabolic Parameters of Overweight Night Workers without Cardiometabolic Abnormalities.
papers.abstract: Night workers are chronically exposed to circadian disruption and melatonin suppression, conditions associated with an increased risk of cardiometabolic disorders. To determine whether exogenous melatonin administration impacts cardiometabolic parameters (glucose, glycated hemoglobin [HbA1c], insulin, total cholesterol, high-density lipoprotein [HDL], low-density lipoprotein [LDL], very low-density lipoprotein [VLDL], triglycerides, heart rates, and mean systolic and diastolic blood pressure) in overweight night workers without cardiometabolic abnormalities. A randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, crossover trial was conducted. Participants (n = 27) took 3 mg of fast-release melatonin or placebo orally for 3 months, 1 hour before bedtime, only on days off when they had nocturnal sleep, on an intermittent basis (every other day). Generalized estimating equations (GEEs) were used to analyze the cardiometabolic parameters. Systolic blood pressure showed a significant effect of time ( p = 0.01). Bonferroni-adjusted post-hoc comparisons showed higher values after placebo than at baseline (mean difference: 5.82 mmHg; 95%CI: 2.02-9.62; adjusted p = 0.01), whereas the difference between melatonin and placebo was not statistically significant (adjusted p = 1.00). No statistically significant effects of time were detected for the other cardiometabolic parameters. Melatonin was not associated with significant changes in cardiometabolic parameters compared with placebo in overweight night workers.

papers.title: Exploring the Association of Fear, Mental Health, and Lifestyle with Insomnia: A Machine Learning Approach among University Students.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to identify key predictors of insomnia among university students, focusing on psychological, behavioral, and lifestyle factors. The study also aimed to explore the role of machine learning in identifying insomnia-related patterns and informing personalized intervention strategies. A cross-sectional study was conducted with 576 students from universities in Birjand during the 2023-2024 academic year. Machine learning methods, including Random Forest, Decision Tree, and SHAP analysis, were used for feature importance analysis and knowledge extraction. Self-reported questionnaires revealed that fear of not falling asleep particularly in the late hours and stress were the most significant predictors of insomnia. Anxiety, poor sleep hygiene, and depression were also strongly associated with insomnia. Other associated factors included financial and family concerns, bedtime, wake-up time, sleep duration, and social media usage. Machine learning models further highlighted these factors, with those showing poor sleep hygiene and high anxiety levels being more likely to experience insomnia. The findings underscore the complex relationship between mental health issues and sleep disorders, particularly insomnia, in university students. The results also suggest a bidirectional relationship between insomnia, anxiety, depression, and stress. The use of machine learning showed potential for identifying insomnia-related patterns and informing personalized intervention strategies. These results highlight the need for effective strategies to address insomnia in students, particularly in light of the growing stressors faced in academic and personal life. However, due to the cross-sectional design, causal inferences cannot be drawn.

papers.title: Rapid Eye Movement Sleep Behavior Disorder as a Prodromal Manifestation of Alpha-Synucleinopathies.
papers.abstract: Rapid eye movement (REM) sleep behavior disorder (RBD) is a parasomnia in which patients physically act out their dreams due to loss of the normal muscle paralysis that occurs during REM sleep. It is now recognized that isolated RBD (iRBD) is strongly associated with future development of α-synuclein-related neurodegenerative diseases, including Parkinson disease (PD), dementia with Lewy bodies (DLB), and multiple system atrophy (MSA). It is seen that most patients with polysomnography-confirmed iRBD eventually develop a clinically defined synucleinopathy, often after a long symptom-free interval. This long prodromal phase makes iRBD a unique clinical model for studying the earliest stages of neurodegeneration, before the onset of clear motor or cognitive disability. α-synuclein pathology frequently begins in the lower brainstem and autonomic nervous system, affecting REM sleep regulatory circuits early in the disease process. As pathology spreads, dopaminergic, cholinergic, and cortical systems become involved, leading to the gradual emergence of motor, autonomic, and cognitive symptoms. As a result, many individuals with iRBD exhibit subtle non-motor features such as hyposmia, constipation, orthostatic hypotension, anxiety, and mild cognitive changes years before a formal neurological diagnosis is made. Recent advances have improved the ability to identify patients at the highest risk of near-term phenoconversion. Quantitative measures of REM sleep without atonia, dopamine transporter imaging, autonomic testing, and emerging molecular biomarkers, including α-synuclein seed amplification assays, have shown promise in risk stratification. In addition, cognitive changes may occur earlier than previously recognized, particularly in patients with iRBD who also demonstrate hyposmia or dopaminergic dysfunction. Management of RBD remains largely symptomatic and focuses on injury prevention and sleep stabilization. While clonazepam and melatonin remain first-line therapies, alternative treatments including sodium oxybate, serotonergic agents, cannabinoids, and modulation of the gut-brain axis through probiotic supplementation have also been explored. This narrative review summarizes current knowledge regarding the clinical features, mechanisms, biomarkers, and management of RBD as a prodromal manifestation of α-synucleinopathies, with emphasis on its importance for early diagnosis and future disease-modifying research.
keywords: rapid eye movement sleep behaviour disorder

papers.title: Associations Between Psychological Factors, Routine Hematological and Biochemical Indicators, and Non-Suicidal Self-Injury Among University Students: An Exploratory Cross-Sectional Study.
papers.abstract: Non-suicidal self-injury (NSSI) is a major mental health concern among university students. Although psychological risk factors for NSSI have been extensively studied, the potential contribution of routinely available hematological and biochemical indicators remains unclear. This study examined their associations with NSSI and their incremental value beyond psychological factors. This cross-sectional study included 1,661 university students who completed campus psychological screening and routine health examinations. NSSI status was defined as an NSSI total score greater than zero. Psychological variables included depressive symptoms, anxiety symptoms, sleep problems, impulsivity, attentional control, cognitive emotion regulation strategies, and problematic internet use. Associations between routine indicators and NSSI severity were examined using Spearman correlations, while logistic regression models evaluated associations with NSSI status after adjustment for demographic and psychological factors. Five-fold cross-validation was used to compare predictive performance across demographic, routine indicator, psychological, and combined models. Among the 1,661 participants, 244 (14.69%) were classified as having NSSI. Several routine indicators, including AST, ALT, red blood cell count, uric acid, hemoglobin, and hematocrit, showed weak correlations with NSSI total scores after FDR correction. However, no routine hematological or biochemical indicator remained significant after false discovery rate (FDR) correction in either adjusted logistic regression model. The psychological model showed substantially better predictive performance than demographic or routine indicator models, and adding routine indicators did not improve prediction (AUC: 0.796 vs. 0.787). Routine hematological and biochemical indicators showed weak associations with NSSI severity but provided limited incremental value beyond psychological factors for identifying NSSI among university students. Psychological assessment remains an important component of NSSI screening, whereas routine laboratory data did not show additional incremental value in this sample.

papers.title: Symptom and Quality-Of-Life Trajectories After High-Intensity Focused Ultrasound in Patients with Advanced Cancer: Exploratory Associations with Overall Survival in a Prospective Pilot Study.
papers.abstract: Patients with advanced cancer frequently experience substantial symptom burden and impaired quality of life (QoL). This study aimed to characterize longitudinal trajectories of patient-reported symptoms and QoL after high-intensity focused ultrasound (HIFU) and to explore their associations with subsequent overall survival (OS). This exploratory prospective longitudinal pilot cohort study enrolled 54 patients with malignant solid tumors who underwent HIFU. Patient-reported symptoms and QoL were assessed using a study-specific 14-item symptom checklist and the EORTC QLQ-C30 at five post-HIFU time points: day 1 (D1), week 1, month 1 (M1), month 2, and month 3. Longitudinal outcomes were summarized descriptively. Exploratory associations with OS were examined using Kaplan-Meier analyses and univariable Cox proportional hazards models. At D1, the most prevalent symptoms were sleep disturbance (55.56%), back pain (44.44%), dry mouth (35.19%), hiccup (29.63%), and dysphoria (25.93%). The mean severity scores of the five most severe symptoms at D1 reached their lowest observed values at M1, while QoL reached its highest observed mean score at M1 (77.41). Median OS was 298 days (95% CI, 209 days to not reached). In exploratory univariable Cox analyses, back pain at D1 (HR = 2.25, 95% CI 1.13-4.47; p = 0.021) and hiccup at D1 (HR = 2.12, 95% CI 1.06-4.24; p = 0.034) were associated with a higher hazard of death. Each 10-point increase in global health status/QoL at D1 was associated with a lower hazard of death (HR = 0.81, 95% CI 0.68-0.98; p = 0.024). In this exploratory pilot cohort, several patient-reported symptoms and QoL measures showed their most favorable observed values at approximately one month after HIFU. Back pain, hiccup, and QoL showed exploratory associations with OS. These preliminary findings may inform post-HIFU symptom and QoL assessment and warrant validation in larger prospective studies.

papers.title: The association study between dietary behaviors, lifestyle patterns and comorbid depressive and anxiety symptoms in Yunnan adolescents aged 12-19, Southwest China: a largescale cross-section screen and a propensity score matching analysis.
papers.abstract: The purpose of this study is to explore the association of dietary behaviors and other lifestyle habits with the presence of comorbid depressive and anxiety symptoms in adolescents aged from 12 to 19 years old in Yunnan Province in Southwest China. We conducted a complex, multi-stage stratified, probability sampling design in 57,031 participants from 253 multi-center of 129 counties of Yunnan in 2023. Participants with complete information on basic demographic information, dietary behaviors, lifestyle patterns (incuding sleep duration, screen time, and exercises etc.,), and who participated in the survey and assessed depressive and anxiety symptoms using standardized measures. Propensity score matching was performed to reduce imbalance in prespecified measured covariates between comparison groups. Multivariable logistic regression models were used to examine the association. The detection rate of total participants in the comorbid depressive and anxiety symptoms was 12.72%. And the detection rate of females in the comorbid depressive and anxiety symptoms group (15.51%) was notably higher than that of males (9.73%). After controlling for potential confounding effects through multiple logistic regression analyses, and after PSM, sedative medication misuse (OR = 4.613, 95% CI 3.734-5.699), the use of electronic devices in dark environments at night (always using: OR = 3.538, 95% CI 3.111-4.023), computer use exceeding 2 h daily (OR = 1.719, 95% CI 1.499-1.971), insufficient sleep (OR= 1.600, 95% CI 1.456-1.757), smoking (OR = 1.469, 95% CI 1.339-1.612) and alcohol consumption (OR = 1.706, 95% CI 1.572-1.851) were positive association. Consuming breakfast (OR = 0.450, 95% CI 0.380-0.532), vegetables (OR = 0.712, 95% CI 0.587-0.864), and fruits (OR = 0.705, 95% CI 0.618-0.805), the computer use < 2 h daily (OR = 0.866, 95% CI 0.801-0.936) and watching TV < 2 h (OR = 0.771, 95% CI 0.706-0.843) were negative association. Healthy dietary, sleep patterns, and digital device usage should be carefully monitored as part of adolescent mental health interventions. And longitudinal, culturally responsive, and comprehensive interventions addressing individual behaviors, family dynamics, and community-level factors are urgently needed.

papers.title: Comparison of Commercial Fixed and In-House Tissue-Based and Live Cell-Based Assays for the Detection of Common Neuronal Surface Autoantibodies.
papers.abstract: Autoimmune encephalitis (AIE) is diagnosed through detection of neuronal-surface antibodies (Abs) in serum and/or cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). Commercial biochip-based cell-based assay (CBA) using fixed cells and in-house CBAs using live cells may give incongruent results. We aimed to shed further light on features of AIE patients with discordant CBA results to establish factors related with diagnosis and treatment-response. A total of 45 patients found positive for N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor (NMDAR), leucine rich glioma inactivated 1 (LGI1), contactin-associated protein-like 2 (CASPR2)-Abs on routine screening done with fixed-CBA, were further tested using in-house live-CBA and tissue-based assay (TBA). Serum neurofilament light chain (NFL) levels were measured and response to immunotherapy was assessed in a follow-up period of 36.9±7.8 months. Thirty patients who were positive on both fixed and live-CBA/TBA, showed trends towards displaying limbic symptoms and EEG/MRI features suggestive of AIE. By contrast, most of the 15 patients with only fixed-CBA positivity failed to fulfill AIE criteria. Positivity on live CBA/TBA did not predict response to immunotherapy or coexisting cancers. Some patients in the fixed-CBA positive category exhibited features highly suggestive of autoimmune encephalopathy and elevated NFL levels. Lower disease severity, presence of viral prodromal findings, absence of autonomic symptoms and facial dyskinesia were associated with treatment response. Live CBA/TBA demonstrated higher diagnostic accuracy than fixed cell-based assays and substantially reduced the likelihood of false-positive antibody detection. Positive live-CBA/TBA results strongly coincide with definite AIE criteria. However, live CBA and NFL results fail to predict response to immunotherapy and identify coexisting cancers. This is putatively because some patients in the live-CBA/TBA negative category likely have immunotherapy-responsive neuroinflammatory disorders.

papers.title: Social Media Use and Emotional Reactivity to Negative Stimuli: An ERP Investigation.
papers.abstract: Exposure to violent media has long been associated with reduced emotional reactivity, empathy, and moral sensitivity, which is a phenomenon commonly referred to as emotional desensitization. Although numerous studies have explored this process in video games and films, its neural correlates in social media contexts remain insufficiently examined. This study aimed to examine whether individual differences in social media use are associated with neural responses to negative emotional stimuli. Fifty-six healthy young adults participated in an electroencephalography (EEG) experiment, during which they passively viewed negative, neutral, and positive images selected from the International Affective Picture System (IAPS). Emotional processing was assessed using two event-related potential (ERP) components: the Early Posterior Negativity (EPN, 200-300 ms) and the Late Positive Potential (LPP, 300-800 ms). Amplitude differences across stimulus categories and brain regions were analyzed using repeated-measures ANOVA. Negative images elicited significantly greater LPP amplitudes compared to neutral and positive images, particularly across central, parietal, and temporal regions, indicating sustained emotional engagement. In contrast, EPN amplitudes did not differ significantly across conditions, suggesting that early attentional mechanisms were not modulated by emotional valence. No group differences were observed between participants with high and low levels of social media use. The findings indicate that typical social media exposure was not associated with reduced neural responsiveness in this sample. Emotional engagement with negative stimuli remains intact, supporting the notion that desensitization is a gradual, context-dependent process influenced by the nature and intensity of digital exposure.

papers.title: Adverse childhood experiences, lifestyle-related risks, and suicidal ideation and suicide attempts among Chinese college students: joint associations and exploratory network analysis.
papers.abstract: Adverse childhood experiences (ACEs) are established correlates of suicidality, but their joint associations with cumulative lifestyle-related risks during emerging adulthood and the conditional connections among specific indicators remain insufficiently characterized. A cross-sectional survey was conducted among 18,723 college students selected through multistage cluster sampling from six colleges in Shaanxi Province, China. Thirteen ACE domains were assessed using the Adverse Childhood Experiences International Questionnaire. A cumulative lifestyle-related risk score included smoking, drinking, inadequate physical activity, unhealthy body mass index, and unhealthy diet. Suicidal ideation (SI) and suicide attempt (SA) during the past 12 months were self-reported. Modified Poisson regression was used to estimate adjusted prevalence ratios (aPRs). Departure from additivity on the prevalence-ratio scale was evaluated using the relative excess risk due to interaction (RERI) and attributable proportion (AP). Exploratory network models were used to characterize conditional associations and cross-community connectivity. The prevalence of SI and SA was 3.3 and 1.9% during the past 12 months, respectively. Greater ACE exposure and higher cumulative lifestyle-related risk score were associated with a higher prevalence of both outcomes. Compared with participants reporting 0-3 ACEs and 0-1 lifestyle-related risk factors, those reporting ≥4 ACEs and ≥2 lifestyle-related risks had the highest adjusted prevalence ratios of SI (aPR, 8.37; 95% CI, 5.64-11.10) and SA (aPR, 10.30; 95% CI, 5.76-14.85). Positive departure from additivity was observed for SI (RERI, 3.35; 95% CI, 1.03-5.97; AP, 0.40; 95% CI, 0.13-0.62) and SA (RERI, 5.18; 95% CI, 1.92-9.78; AP, 0.50; 95% CI, 0.19-0.75). In the exploratory networks, poor sleep showed high cross-community connectivity, while emotional abuse, bullying, inadequate physical activity, and drinking also showed prominent bridge expected influence. Greater ACE exposure and cumulative lifestyle-related risks were separately and jointly associated with a higher prevalence of SI and SA. Participants reporting both ≥ 4 ACEs and ≥2 lifestyle-related risk profiles had the highest prevalence for SI and SA with evidence of additive interactions. The network results describe cross-sectional conditional associations and should be regarded as hypothesis-generating rather than as evidence of causal or mediating pathways.

papers.title: Self-Guided Beta-Responsive Visual Neurofeedback in a Public Exhibition: Feasibility and Usability Randomized Controlled rial.
papers.abstract: Neurofeedback is studied for stress and anxiety regulation, but most systems require supervision or research-grade equipment. Consumer electroencephalography (EEG) could broaden access, yet autonomous first-contact feasibility, usability, and baseline neural-state effects remain unclear. We assessed autonomous completion and usability, tested whether a fixed breathing pacer improved outcomes over visual neurofeedback alone, and explored whether pretask resting beta was associated with usability. We conducted a single-session, 2-arm randomized feasibility and usability trial at a public science exhibition in Bern, Switzerland, between March and June 2025. Eligible adults were aged 18 years or older, could read German or French, and reported no epilepsy or implanted electronic device. A tablet app guided participants without experimenter assistance through consent, setup, a 30-second eyes-closed baseline, 1:1 randomization, a 120-second beta-responsive task, and questionnaires. The final analytic sample included participants assigned to visual neurofeedback only (VN; n=27) or visual neurofeedback plus a 6 breaths/minute breathing pacer (VN+BP; n=25). Outcomes were usability, relaxation, and state mindfulness. Data were collected prospectively; no secondary data were used. Analyses used Mann-Whitney U, chi-square, Spearman, and permutation tests (2-sided, α=.05); EEG outcome and item analyses were exploratory. Of 110 visitors initiating a session, 79 completed the task with a valid EEG recording (71.8%, 95% CI 62.8-79.4) and 52 met analytic criteria (47.3%, 95% CI 38.2%-56.5%). Participants (35 women) had a mean age of 39.0 (SD 11.3) years. Usability was good (System Usability Scale [SUS] mean 72.3, SD 14.7; 95% CI 68.3-76.2), and 31/52 participants scored at least 68 (59.6%, 95% CI 46.1%-71.8%). Usability did not differ between VN and VN+BP (median 75.0, IQR 62.5-81.3 vs median 72.5, IQR 65.0-90.0; Mann-Whitney U=362.5, P=.65; rank-biserial r=-0.07, 95% CI -0.39 to 0.25). Relaxation (median 63.0, IQR 50.0-80.0 vs median 61.0, IQR 50.0-67.0; Mann-Whitney U=276.5, P=.27; r=0.18, 95% CI -0.14 to 0.49) and mindfulness (median 2.4, IQR 2.1-2.8 vs median 2.5, IQR 2.0-3.2; Mann-Whitney U=346.5, P=.68; r=-0.07, 95% CI -0.39 to 0.26) did not differ. Higher resting beta was associated with lower SUS before correction (Spearman ρ=-0.31, 95% CI -0.54 to -0.04; raw P=.03), but not after Benjamini-Hochberg correction (adjusted P=.30). SUS item analyses showed a global pattern (permutation P=.02), strongest for functional integration (ρ=-0.43, 95% CI -0.63 to -0.18; Holm-adjusted P=.01). This trial evaluated an autonomous consumer-EEG neurofeedback system integrating self-fitting, signal-quality checking, baseline calibration, adaptive feedback, randomization, and self-report without operator support. Many first-time users completed the autonomous workflow with acceptable-to-good usability; a fixed, open-loop breathing pacer did not improve usability, relaxation, or state mindfulness; and higher resting beta showed a preliminary association with lower perceived usability. These findings support autonomous consumer-EEG neurofeedback and motivate work on adaptive onboarding, validated EEG pipelines, and objective self-regulation outcomes.

papers.title: Assessing affective states in domestic dogs through judgment bias tasks: a systematic review of methods, influencing factors, and welfare applications.
papers.abstract: Judgment bias tasks (JBTs) have emerged as a promising approach for assessing affective states in animals, including domestic dogs, by measuring optimistic or pessimistic responses to ambiguous stimuli as proxies for underlying emotion. Despite growing use, the canine evidence base had not been systematically evaluated. We conducted a systematic review following PRISMA 2020 guidelines, searching Scopus and PubMed, with a supplementary search of Web of Science Core Collection. Thirty-two studies (15 experimental, 13 observational/quasi-experimental, 4 methodological) met the inclusion criteria. Experimental studies were appraised with the SYRCLE risk-of-bias tool. Findings were synthesized narratively, as methodological heterogeneity precluded meta-analysis. Five paradigm types were identified, but 28 of the 32 studies (88%) used the same spatial discrimination task; the four remaining paradigms were represented by one study each. JBTs showed sensitivity to some experimental manipulations, including oxytocin (d = 2.16) and environmental enrichment (nosework, p < 0.01), while observational and quasi-experimental studies also reported associations between training method and JBT performance (e.g., aversive versus reward-based training: Z = -2.38, p = 0.017). However, validity and reliability concerns were pervasive: ceiling effects at ambiguous locations, confounding by spatial-learning ability, poor test-retest reliability, and absent protocol standardization. Convergence with independent welfare indicators was only partial. JBTs are responsive to some affective manipulations and are associated with relevant welfare and experiential factors, but substantial validity and reliability limitations remain. Standardized protocols and multi-method validation are needed before JBTs can serve as field measures of canine welfare.

papers.title: Efficacy and safety of commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations combined with biomedicine for elderly patients with primary insomnia: a systematic review and meta-analysis of randomized controlled trials.
papers.abstract: The prevalence of primary insomnia among the elderly is steadily increasing; however, robust evidence supporting the efficacy and safety of combining commercial Chinese polyherbal preparations (CCPPs) with biomedicine therapy remains insufficient. This study aimed to systematically evaluate the efficacy and safety of CCPPs combined with biomedicine versus biomedicine therapy for primary insomnia in elderly patients, and to assess the certainty of the evidence via the GRADE framework and P-curve analysis. Seven biomedical databases were searched (before November 2025) for randomized controlled trials (RCTs) involving elderly patients with primary insomnia. Risk of bias was assessed using Cochrane RoB 2 by two researchers independently. Meta-analysis was performed using R software. Outcomes included Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), total clinical effectiveness rate, Sleep Dysfunction Rating Scale (SDRS), and adverse events. Robustness was evaluated via sensitivity, subgroup, and P-curve analyses. Meta-analysis suggested that combined therapy was associated with a lower PSQI score (MD = -2.09, 95% CI -2.62 to -1.57) and higher total clinical effectiveness rate (RR = 1.21, 95% CI 1.15-1.27) relative to monotherapy. The combination group also showed a lower risk of adverse events (RR = 0.47, 95% CI 0.36-0.61). However, P-curve analysis revealed notable discrepancies across outcomes: PSQI exhibited sufficient evidential value (Power = 99%), whereas the total clinical effectiveness rate lacked adequate evidential value (Power = 9%), implying potential publication bias. Subgroup analyses showed that heterogeneity decreased within the subgroup of patients with disease duration <1 year, although the between-subgroup difference did not reach statistical significance. The certainty of evidence was rated as "Moderate" for adverse events but "Low" to "Very Low" for efficacy outcomes. In elderly patients with primary insomnia, combined treatment of CCPPs and biomedicine may help improve sleep quality and may reduce adverse events reported in clinical trials. However, due to methodological limitations, high heterogeneity and potential publication bias among the included trials, the certainty of the available evidence remains limited. Given insufficient evidential value, the reliability of the total clinical effectiveness rate is questionable, and clinicians should place greater emphasis on outcomes assessed using validated scales such as the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Further large-scale, multicenter, double-blind, placebo-controlled randomized controlled trials (RCTs) are needed to further verify these preliminary findings. https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251186213, identifier: CRD420251186213.

papers.title: Central Adiposity and Tear Film Instability in Adults With Obesity.
papers.abstract: To examine the association between central adiposity, assessed by waist-to-height ratio (WHtR), and tear film stability in adults with obesity. This cross-sectional observational study included 269 adults with BMI ≥ 28 kg/m2. WHtR and noninvasive tear breakup time (NIBUT) were the primary exposure and outcome. Models adjusted for age, sex, education, systemic diseases, myopia, display exposure, smoking, alcohol consumption, and sleep problems. Secondary outcomes were Ocular Surface Disease Index (OSDI) and dry eye disease (DED) status; other adiposity indices were examined in separate models. Each 1-SD higher WHtR was associated with shorter NIBUT (adjusted β -0.341 s; 95% CI -0.612--0.071; p = 0.014). The highest versus lowest WHtR tertile differed by -0.961 s (95% CI -1.696--0.227). BMI had a numerically larger coefficient (-0.591 s; 95% CI -0.842--0.339). DED was present in 208 participants (77.3%). The WHtR-DED association was nominally significant (OR 1.630; 95% CI 1.072-2.477; p = 0.022) but did not survive false discovery rate correction (q = 0.061). Higher WHtR was associated with modestly shorter NIBUT among adults with obesity, while BMI showed a numerically larger association. These findings support considering overall and abdominal adiposity in the clinical assessment of ocular surface function.

papers.title: Pain Management in Orthopedic Surgery: A Procedure-Specific Orthopedic-Anesthesia Approach to Perioperative Analgesia.
papers.abstract: Introduction: Post-operative pain in orthopedic surgery is clinically important because inadequate analgesia can impair mobilization, sleep, physiotherapy and discharge, while excessive analgesia can cause sedation, motor weakness, drug toxicity and unnecessary opioid exposure. This narrative review uses a structured literature search of PubMed/MEDLINE and targeted review of recent systematic reviews, randomized trials, consensus statements and procedure-specific recommendations, with emphasis on publications available through September 2026. Evidence is synthesized qualitatively according to procedure, analgesic strategy, functional outcomes, and limitations of the underlying evidence. Present evidence supports multimodal analgesia, but does not support a universal regimen or routine addition of every available intervention. Regional techniques can improve early analgesia, although benefits vary by procedure and may be offset by motor block, rebound pain, or limitations in post-operative examination. A non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) provide opioid-sparing analgesia, but the relationship between NSAID exposure and fracture healing remains uncertain and appears to depend on drug, dose, duration, fracture type, and patient factors. Opioids remain appropriate as rescue therapy when clinically indicated. Persistent post-surgical pain is influenced by pre-operative and biopsychosocial factors and acute analgesia has not been shown consistently to prevent it. The practical framework proposed here therefore links the operation, patient risk profile, analgesic options, and rehabilitation task, with unexpected severe pain treated as a trigger for clinical reassessment rather than automatic escalation.

papers.title: Don't sleep on the other beds: Atherosclerosis across heart, brain, and limbs.
Rethinking adult primary snoring: from diagnostic ambiguity to phenotype-informed, patient-centered care.
Artificial intelligence-generated and algorithmically personalized music interventions and their effects on brain function, behavior, and health: a critical review.
papers.abstract: This critical review synthesizes empirical studies of algorithmically personalized and artificial-intelligence-generated music interventions reporting neurophysiological, neuroimaging, or objective behavioral outcomes. Literature was identified through structured searches of PubMed, Scopus, Google Scholar, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library through 12 August 2026, with CNKI and Wanfang searched on 22 September 2026, supplemented by citation tracking. Twenty-one eligible studies (at least 1,005 participants) were identified. Five things the term artificial intelligence covers in this literature are separated: algorithmic selection from a corpus, rule-based sonification, parametric modulation of pre-existing material, machine-learning generative composition, and closed-loop delivery contingent on the listener's own signal. Only three studies used a machine-learning generative model, so most of the evidence concerns algorithmic personalization of existing material. Studies of closed-loop neural systems reported the most consistent neurophysiological signal, and music-based alpha neurofeedback produced higher normalized alpha power than yoked random feedback. In an open-loop design, personalized EEG-derived music was reported to attenuate anxiety induction where self-selected preferred music and silence did not, with enhanced prefrontal theta oscillations as the associated correlate. Eight studies carried a comparator capable of isolating an algorithmic component from music exposure, and all eight favored the algorithmic condition. These eight address different causal questions, use different designs, and point to no single mechanism, so their results are best read as preliminary and hypothesis-generating. Evidence quality was very low throughout. The median reported sample size was 22, no study blinded participants or measured expectancy, and no specific finding has been independently replicated. GRADE certainty was very low for every outcome domain, covering EEG oscillatory power, sleep architecture, autonomic regulation, epileptiform activity, and cognitive, behavioral and affective outcomes. Neurophysiological change is reported more often than behavioral change, and behavioral change more often than clinical benefit. The evidence supports continued investigation and does not support clinical deployment. Eight reporting and design requirements for future trials are proposed.

papers.title: Factors associated with postoperative sleep disturbance in patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Postoperative sleep disturbance (PSD) is common in patients following surgery, resulting in severe cognitive and mood disturbances, and even increase mortality risk. This study aimed to identify factors associated with PSD in patients undergoing thoracoscopic radical resection for lung cancer. We retrospectively identified sixty-two patients who underwent thoracoscopic radical resection of lung cancer at Tangdu Hospital, a tertiary teaching hospital in Xi'an, China, from June 2023 through October 2024. PSD was defined as a Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) score <60 on postoperative day 2 (POD2). Preoperative sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Pain was measured using the Numeric Rating Scale (NRS) at rest and during coughing on POD1 and POD2. intraoperative fluid volume, and POD2 cough-induced pain, selected a priori based on clinical relevance and prior evidence. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed to identify factors independently associated with PSD. Of 62 patients (mean age 67.5 years; 45.2% female), 36 (58.1%) met the RCSQ-defined criteria for PSD on POD2. Three factors were independently associated with PSD: preoperative PSQI score [odds ratio (OR) =1.58, 95% confidence interval (CI): 1.19-2.10, P=0.001], intraoperative fluid volume (OR =1.004 per mL, 95% CI: 1.001-1.007, P=0.02), and POD2 cough-induced pain (OR =2.23 per point, 95% CI: 1.36-3.66, P=0.001). The model demonstrated good calibration (Hosmer-Lemeshow P=0.10) and discrimination (Nagelkerke R2=0.652). Preoperative sleep quality, intraoperative fluid volume, and POD2 cough-induced pain were independently associated with PSD in this cohort. These exploratory findings highlight the importance of closer assessment of potentially high-risk patients, but require validation in larger prospective studies before being translated into definitive preventive strategies.

papers.title: Adult primary snoring: a modified Delphi consensus among Chinese otolaryngologists with AI-assisted evidence synthesis.
papers.abstract: Primary snoring is common in adults, but its definition, diagnostic boundaries, and management remain inconsistent. Misclassification between primary snoring and mild obstructive sleep apnea may expose patients to either unnecessary treatment or inadequate evaluation. This expert consensus aimed to develop an evidence-informed framework for adult primary snoring that emphasizes objective exclusion of obstructive sleep apnea and patient- and bed-partner-centered outcomes. A modified Delphi study enrolled a purposive panel of 30 experts in otolaryngology-head and neck surgery and sleep medicine from five Chinese regions. A 25-source targeted evidence corpus, supplemented by question-driven searches and human-verified artificial intelligence-assisted extraction, informed 75 unique candidate items. Four anonymous online rounds used a 9-point scale; consensus was predefined as at least 80% agreement and strong consensus as at least 90%. A pragmatic three-level evidence-basis label distinguished direct evidence from indirect evidence and expert consensus. Round response rates were 93.3% (28/30), 96.7% (29/30), 96.7% (29/30), and 96.7% (29/30). Of 75 unique candidate items, 68 reached consensus; consolidation yielded 54 final statements and seven explicit non-consensus items. The framework separates clinically suspected from objectively confirmed primary snoring, addresses night-to-night diagnostic variability, and prioritizes patient- and bed-partner-centered outcomes. First-line care is proportional and phenotype-informed; custom titratable mandibular advancement devices are the preferred device-based option for suitable patients, while surgery is restricted to selected anatomical targets. This consensus provides a transparent, risk-stratified framework for adult primary snoring and identifies unresolved controversies. Multidisciplinary external validation, standardized outcome definitions, and prospective phenotype-stratified trials are required before broad international adoption.

papers.title: Uncontrolled metabolic syndrome associated with poorer sleep quality in adults in rural areas: a secondary analysis.
papers.abstract: To examine whether clinical management of metabolic syndrome (MetS) is associated with sleep health among adults receiving care in rural primary care settings. This cross-sectional analysis used baseline data from adults (age 20-75 years; body mass index (BMI) 30-45 kg/m2) enrolled in the RE-POWER trial, a pragmatic behavioral weight loss intervention implemented in rural primary care clinics. Sleep quality was assessed using the Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). MetS was defined according to American Heart Association/National Heart, Lung, and Blood Institute (AHA/NHLBI) criteria and categorized as: (1) no-MetS, (2) controlled MetS (criteria met via medication use), and (3) uncontrolled MetS (criteria met via abnormal laboratory values). Linear mixed models evaluated whether MetS status predicted global PSQI, PSQI subcomponents, and sleep duration, adjusting for age, sex, and BMI. Among 1406 adults (mean age 54.6 ± 11.8 years; 76.8% female), those with uncontrolled MetS (n = 634) had significantly worse global PSQI, sleep latency, and sleep disturbance scores compared with adults without MetS (n = 483) (P < .05). Sleep outcomes did not differ between adults with controlled MetS (n = 289) and those without MetS (P > .05). Poorly controlled MetS was associated with poorer sleep quality, whereas clinically controlled MetS was not. Future research is needed to determine if effective clinical management of MetS may confer benefits for sleep health in rural populations.

papers.title: Comparison of short-term peripheral nerve stimulation, single-target supraorbital nerve pulsed radiofrequency, and dual-target supraorbital nerve-stellate ganglion pulsed radiofrequency for herpes zoster ophthalmicus-associated pain: a retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: To compare the clinical outcomes of short-term peripheral nerve stimulation (st-PNS), supraorbital nerve pulsed radiofrequency (SON-PRF), and combined supraorbital nerve and stellate ganglion pulsed radiofrequency (SON + SG-PRF) for herpes zoster ophthalmicus (HZO)-associated pain. This retrospective study included patients with HZO-associated pain who underwent st-PNS, SON-PRF, or SON + SG-PRF between January 2023 and January 2026. The primary outcome was the longitudinal change in Numerical Rating Scale (NRS) scores over 24 weeks. Secondary outcomes included the clinical response rate, anxiety (GAD-7), depression (PHQ-9), sleep quality (PSQI), and treatment-related adverse events. The incidence of postherpetic neuralgia (PHN) was assessed as an exploratory outcome only in patients with a disease duration of ≤90 days at treatment. Longitudinal outcomes were analyzed using baseline-adjusted linear mixed-effects models, with propensity score weighting used for sensitivity analyses. A total of 269 patients were included: 84 in the st-PNS group, 96 in the SON-PRF group, and 89 in the SON + SG-PRF group. NRS scores decreased over follow-up in all three groups. In the primary and both propensity score-weighted analyses, the overall NRS trajectory was lower with st-PNS than with SON-PRF, whereas no significant difference was observed between st-PNS and SON + SG-PRF. The overall GAD-7 trajectory was lower with SON + SG-PRF than with SON-PRF, and the overall PSQI trajectory was lower with SON + SG-PRF than with either st-PNS or SON-PRF; these differences remained statistically significant in both weighted analyses. The overall trajectories of depressive symptoms did not differ significantly among the groups. Exploratory analysis did not establish a difference in PHN risk among the three groups. No serious treatment-related adverse events occurred during follow-up. To our knowledge, this study is the first to compare multidimensional clinical outcomes of st-PNS, SON-PRF, and SON + SG-PRF for HZO-associated pain within the same cohort. st-PNS showed a relatively consistent analgesic benefit over SON-PRF, whereas SON + SG-PRF also provided analgesia and showed potential benefits for anxiety and sleep outcomes. These findings require confirmation in prospective studies.

papers.title: The relationship between sleep problems and well-being among Chinese children: a moderated mediation model with anxiety as mediator and resilience as moderator.
papers.abstract: Prior research has shown that well-being is a key factor in children's developmental outcomes. However, the factors that relate to children's well-being are still unclear, especially among Chinese populations. This research investigated the relationship between sleep problems and the well-being of children in China, specifically testing (1) whether sleep problems were associated with well-being, (2) whether anxiety may serve as a mediator, and (3) whether resilience may moderate this association. A total of 606 Chinese children (53.3% girls; mean age = 11.09 years) participated in the present study using a cross-sectional design by completing self-report instruments, including the Athens Insomnia Scale, the Oxford Happiness Questionnaire, the Anxiety subscale of the Depression Anxiety Stress Scale, and the Connor-Davidson Resilience Scale. Pearson correlations and a moderated mediation analysis using PROCESS Model 58 with 5,000 bootstrap samples were conducted, controlling for age. (1) There was a significant negative correlation between sleep problems and well-being (r = -0.39, p < 0.001). (2) After controlling for age, anxiety mediated this association. (3) Resilience moderated this association. Specifically, the indirect effect was stronger in the high-resilience group (indirect effect = -0.15, 95% CI = [-0.23, -0.08]) than in the low-resilience group (indirect effect = -0.05, 95% CI = [-0.09, -0.03]). These findings provide preliminary evidence on how sleep problems are associated with well-being among Chinese children. They also suggest that anxiety and resilience may be relevant for future intervention studies, although longitudinal and experimental designs are needed to test whether targeting these factors can improve mental health.

papers.title: The ligament of Marshall as a therapeutic target in atrial fibrillation: from anatomy to catheter-based and surgical management-a narrative review.
papers.abstract: Long regarded as an inconsequential embryological remnant, the ligament of Marshall (LOM) is now recognized as a treatable component of the atrial fibrillation (AF) substrate. This review synthesizes the anatomical, electrophysiological and clinical evidence behind that shift and compares the two routes to the LOM: percutaneous retrograde ethanol infusion into the vein of Marshall (EIVOM) during catheter ablation, and direct division during thoracoscopic surgery. Both act on the same epicardial structure; only the route of access differs. A structured literature search of PubMed, Embase and Web of Science covered the embryology, anatomy, histology and electrophysiology of the LOM and clinical studies of both routes. Two authors screened and selected records independently. Given the heterogeneity of study designs, findings were synthesized narratively. The LOM is a neuro-muscular remnant of the embryonic left superior vena cava that contributes to AF through three mechanisms: triggers arising from insulated myocardial "Marshall bundles", autonomic modulation via adjacent ganglionated plexi, and preferential conduction across the mitral isthmus. Five randomized trials of EIVOM-based strategies have enrolled more than 1,100 patients; pooled analysis shows improved 12-month freedom from any atrial arrhythmia (risk ratio 1.16, 95% confidence interval: 1.04-1.29; number needed to treat 10) and less repeat ablation, without excess major complications (2.5% vs. 2.8%) but with more overall complications and longer fluoroscopy. Crucially, no trial has tested ethanol infusion in isolation; the observed benefit reflects composite lesion sets. Thoracoscopic division interrupts the entire ligament independent of venous anatomy but has never been a randomized variable; randomized evidence for thoracoscopic and hybrid strategies overall ranges from neutral (CASA-AF) to positive (CONVERGE, HARTCAP-AF). Guidelines recognize both as options in selected patients without mandating routine LOM division. The LOM is a reproducible, anatomically defined target reachable percutaneously or by surgical division within a comprehensive AF ablation strategy. The supporting evidence is markedly asymmetric: randomized data exist for EIVOM-based strategies but never for ethanol infusion alone, none at all for surgical division, and the two routes have never been compared head-to-head. Its incremental benefit beyond pulmonary vein and posterior wall isolation remains undefined.

papers.title: Dose-related depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation during cabergoline therapy in an adolescent with macroprolactinoma.
papers.abstract: Cabergoline is the preferred medical treatment for prolactinomas in children and adolescents because of its efficacy in reducing prolactin concentrations and tumor size. Although dopamine agonists are generally well tolerated, neuropsychiatric adverse effects have been reported, with depressive symptoms and suicidal ideation less frequently described. We report a 15-year-old girl with macroprolactinoma who developed low mood, emotional dysregulation, crying spells, reduced appetite, sleep-wake disturbance, loss of interest in previously enjoyable activities, and passive suicidal thoughts after cabergoline was increased to 1 mg twice weekly. She had no previous psychiatric history, major psychosocial stressor, manic symptoms, or psychotic features. Psychiatric assessment identified moderate depressive symptoms, with a Patient Health Questionnaire-9 score of 11. Cabergoline was reduced to 0.75 mg twice weekly because of the close temporal relationship between dose escalation and symptom onset. Her psychiatric symptoms almost completely resolved within a few days, while prolactin remained controlled. The temporal association, apparent dose relationship, and rapid improvement following dose reduction suggest a cabergoline-associated neuropsychiatric adverse reaction. Clinicians should monitor mood and suicidal ideation during dopamine agonist therapy, particularly after dose escalation and in adolescents.

papers.title: Co-creating the EndoWatch - a smart wearable device for the management of hypothalamic dysfunction in pediatric brain tumor survivors: a pilot study.
papers.abstract: Hypothalamic dysfunction (HD) after treatment for a pediatric (supra)sellar tumor severely affects quality of life of patients, as well as their parents and families. Patients may develop signs of fatigue as a result of persistent disturbances in thermoregulation, sleep-wake rhythm, or hormonal insufficiencies. The management of HD requires around-the-clock care by the parent or caregiver. To support patients with HD and their parents/caregivers, we co-created a smart wearable device for continuous monitoring (EndoWatch) to detect early signs of hypothalamic dysregulation. We aimed to evaluate adherence to and user experiences of the first EndoWatch design. In co-creation with clinicians, patient representatives, and design researchers and engineers, an existing smart device (wearable sensor and mobile application (app)) was adapted to a first design tailored for this purpose. In a prospective, observational study, 10 pediatric brain tumor survivors with HD (8 children; 2 adults) tested the first design of the device for 14 days. The primary outcome was adherence to wearing the EndoWatch. Secondary outcomes included usability, learnability, and desirability (through questionnaires), and barriers and facilitators (through semi-structured interviews). Ten patients participated (8 children, mean age 10.8 (SD 3.5); 2 adults, aged 18.9 and 31.0 years). Median overall adherence was 99.4% (IQR 22.8); two patients discontinued early due to wristband-related discomfort. Key facilitators were ease of use of the device and reliable technical performance. Main barriers included the absence of a separate caregiver app and limitations of the patient diary. These findings informed design modifications for future improvements of the device. The concept of the first EndoWatch design was considered acceptable and usable by patients with HD and their caregivers. This study identified key barriers and the modifications required for improvement, which were incorporated into a second EndoWatch design, to be evaluated in a larger prospective study.

papers.title: EEG-SDL-Net: biomedical EEG signal classification via multi-level supervised Kolmogorov-Arnold networks.
papers.abstract: This paper presents a novel supervised deep learning framework for EEG signal classification based on hierarchical one-dimensional convolutional neural networks with Sobel-based temporal enhancement, channel attention, Kolmogorov-Arnold Networks (KAN), and multi-level deep supervision. The proposed framework is designed to improve feature representation, robustness to EEG variability, and computational efficiency for Edge AI deployment. The proposed architecture addresses the challenges of EEG signal variability, nonlinear temporal dynamics, and robust feature extraction. The framework integrates a 1D Sobel projection module for local temporal feature enhancement, a channel-wise attention mechanism for adaptive electrode selection, and KAN to capture complex non-linear relationships. Furthermore, a deep supervision strategy is employed to stabilize training and ensure robust gradient flow. Experimental evaluations on the SEED-VIG dataset demonstrate that the proposed model achieves superior classification accuracy compared to state-of-the-art methods. Performance benchmarks on edge devices, such as the Raspberry Pi 4, show a real-time inference latency of 15 ms, confirming the framework's suitability for Internet of Medical Things (IoMT) and portable monitoring systems. The complete source code has been made openly available and permanently archived through Zenodo: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.21441822.

papers.title: Negative fat talk and sleep quality among Chinese college students: associations involving wellbeing and loneliness.
papers.abstract: This study examined the relationship between negative fat talk and poor sleep quality in Chinese college students, and tested the roles of wellbeing and loneliness in this association. A cross-sectional survey included 2,056 students in Jiangxi Province, China. Negative fat talk, wellbeing, loneliness, physical activity, and sleep quality were assessed with the BTS, WHO-5, ULS-8, PARS-3, and PSQI, respectively. The additional observed-score analyses included 1,970 participants with observed PSQI total scores. The original latent-variable parallel mediation model was retained; a fully adjusted observed-score model was added. The original classification recorded 984 students (47.9% of the study sample) with poor sleep quality. In the original sex-adjusted regression, negative fat talk was associated with higher PSQI scores (standardized β = 0.060, p = 0.003). In the additional fully adjusted regression, its unstandardized coefficient was 0.046 (95%CI 0.016-0.076; p = 0.003). The original structural model reported an overall indirect association of 0.223, with specific associations of 0.118 through wellbeing and 0.105 through loneliness. Negative fat talk was associated with poorer self-reported sleep quality. The parallel indirect paths describe cross-sectional statistical associations.

papers.title: Microecological-metabolic links along the brain-gut-muscle axis in Tuina analgesia from the perspectives of gut metagenomics and untargeted metabolomics.
papers.abstract: Chronic pain involves multilevel processes including central sensitization, peripheral tissue abnormalities, neuroimmune responses, metabolic alterations, and changes in gut microecology. Tuina and related manual therapies can influence local soft-tissue status, peripheral sensory input, autonomic activity, inflammatory responses, and muscle metabolism, whereas the links between their distal systemic effects and gut microecology remain insufficiently characterized. The brain, gut, and skeletal muscle can interact through autonomic pathways, immune-inflammatory signaling, circulating metabolites, myokines, and other distal signals, providing a biological context for analyzing cross-organ changes related to Tuina analgesia. A limited number of studies have reported changes in gut microbiota after Tuina, massage, or combined manual interventions; however, direct evidence continuously linking mechanical stimulation, microbial function, metabolic signaling, and pain improvement remains limited. Gut metagenomics extends analysis beyond species composition to strains, functional genes, and metabolic pathway potential, whereas untargeted metabolomics captures metabolic changes jointly shaped by the host and microbiota. Short-chain fatty acids, bile acids, tryptophan derivatives, and molecules related to lipid and energy metabolism have shown functional associations with neuroimmune regulation, sensory neural activity, and pain sensitization in different pain models. Myokines, metabolites, and extracellular vesicle signals derived from skeletal muscle also provide a possible biological basis for bidirectional gut-muscle communication. Nevertheless, most of these mechanisms originate from studies of pain, the microbiome, or exercise physiology and cannot be directly equated with mechanisms of Tuina analgesia. Integrated metagenomic and metabolomic analyses can identify candidate links involving microbial functions, metabolic alterations, host responses, and pain phenotypes, thereby narrowing the scope of subsequent functional validation. Their interpretation remains influenced by Tuina stimulation parameters, diet, gut transit, medication use, circadian rhythms, and other host factors. Standardization of the intervention, longitudinal multi-omics observation, targeted quantification, functional experiments, and cross-center replication will help clarify the temporal relationships and functional significance of these changes. Microecological-metabolic links across the brain, gut, and skeletal muscle can therefore serve as a cross-organ framework for investigating the systemic effects of Tuina analgesia, although specific pathways and their clinical predictive value still require direct experimental and prospective validation.

papers.title: Lifestyle Medicine: Of Pillars and Pistons, Constructs and Connotations.
papers.abstract: Lifestyle Medicine espouses a framework dividing the field among 6 "pillars:" optimal nutrition, physical activity, restorative sleep, stress management, connectedness, and risky substance avoidance. Pillars, however, though lending support to a common structure, do not interact-they stand apart. Repair to one damaged pillar does nothing to fill the cracks in another. The domains of lifestyle medicine do interact, however, in ways of practical importance to clinician and patient alike. The mismatch between the verbal imagery of a pillar and operational reality of a self-propagating chain reaction has implications for medical practice and personal behavior that make this a matter of more than semantic importance. We make the case that a framework evincing the interactions among the lifestyle medicine domains has the potential to facilitate uptake of relevant practices by showcasing a generally overlooked auto-catalysis and economy of scale. We contend that "pillars" do not reliably and fully convey the value proposition of lifestyle medicine, and suggest some suitable alternatives.

papers.title: Development of Circadian Circuitry Underlying Feeding-Fasting Rhythms in Drosophila Larvae.
papers.abstract: Many organisms do not exhibit strong daily behavioral rhythms early in life. The consolidation of sleep and feeding to specific times of the day does not emerge until later in development. Disruptions to circadian behaviors in early life can lead to dysregulation of both neural development and metabolic homeostasis. However, the circuit mechanisms regulating feeding rhythm development are unknown. Here, we characterize the neural circuitry responsible for driving the development of feeding-fasting rhythms in early 3 rd instar (L3) Drosophila larvae. We find that inactivation of both larval s-LNv circadian pacemaker neurons and SIFamide (SIFa) neurons in the pars intercerebralis disrupts feeding rhythm development. Additionally, our data indicate feeding rhythms likely emerge due to circuit connections forming between s-LNvs and SIFa neurons at the L3 stage. Finally, we show that reductions in signaling between s-LNv and SIFa neurons interfere with normal behavioral rhythm development in L3. Specifically, RNA interference-induced reductions in pigment-dispersing factor ( pdf ) signaling and SIFa signaling disrupt diurnal differences in both feeding and sleep, resulting in a loss of behavioral rhythms. Altogether, our findings identify for the first time the clock and clock output circuitry responsible for feeding rhythm regulation in developing organisms.

papers.title: Longitudinal Associations Between Neighborhood Social Cohesion and Sleep Disturbance Among Older Adults: The Mediating Role of Depressive Symptoms.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbance is highly prevalent in later life and often co-occurs with depressive symptoms. However, the social and psychological factors that contribute to its development remain poorly understood. This longitudinal study examined whether perceived neighborhood social cohesion was associated with subsequent sleep disturbance and whether depressive symptoms mediated this association among older adults. Data were drawn from five waves (2006, 2010, 2014, 2018, and 2022) of the psychosocial subsample of the Health and Retirement Study. The analytic sample comprised 3,360 respondents aged 50 years or older. Univariate and parallel process latent growth curve models were used to examine the developmental trajectory patterns and their associations. A latent growth curve mediation model was further utilized to test the indirect pathways at both the intercept and slope levels. At the intercept level, higher neighborhood social cohesion in 2006 was associated with lower levels of depressive symptoms and sleep disturbance in 2010. The indirect association via depressive symptoms was significant (B = - 0.311, 95% CI [- 0.383, - 0.239]). At the slope level, greater declines in cohesion were associated with greater increases in depressive symptoms (B = - 0.351, 95% CI [- 0.676, - 0.026]), and the indirect path on change in sleep disturbance was also significant (B = - 0.332, 95% CI [- 0.651, - 0.014]). Depressive symptoms may represent an important pathway linking neighborhood social cohesion to sleep disturbance among older adults, highlighting the potential value of strengthening social cohesion and addressing depressive symptoms to promote sleep health.

papers.title: Camus: a video-based framework for continuous behavioral monitoring in the mouse home-cage.
papers.abstract: Home-cage activity is a window into the spontaneous behavioral repertoire of mice. These behaviors are organized across the circadian cycle, and disruptions in their duration, frequency, or organization may provide sensitive measures of neurological or psychiatric dysfunction. While continuous monitoring can help track the dynamics of spontaneous behavior, video recording in conventional laboratory cages is limited by compact cage geometry, opaque cage tops, and obstructed views of animals, food, and water. We therefore developed Camus , a Camera for home-cage recordings of Mus musculus mice. Camus integrates off-the-shelf USB cameras with infrared illumination and custom 3D-printed components for access to food and water without obstructed views. The modular design pairs continuous video acquisition with a manually validated computer-vision model to quantify locomotion, feeding, drinking, and nesting-related behavior across multiday recordings. A single desktop computer can record as many as 20 cages in parallel at an incremental cost of approximately $250 per cage, recording more than 99% of expected frames at 640x360-pixel resolution and 30 frames per second. Camus captured circadian structure in locomotion, feeding, and drinking. Camus also captured nest-building and sex-specific differences in nest dynamics. Using Camus with transgenic 5xFAD mice overexpressing amyloid revealed selective, age-progressive deficits in nesting behavior. Camus provides a scalable, open-source platform that combines accessible hardware, automated video monitoring, and machine-learning based analysis for continuous and potentially longitudinal behavioral phenotyping.
